summary:
Apelle 11 presents itself as a 3D visualization of the Moon, the Sun and Earth. It allows the user to pick a date, a landing site (either by loading it in or by selecting one from the potential future Artemis III landing sites, which are available by default) and a set of conditions they wish to see met on their mission date. The user is then shown the highlighted area of the landing site on the Moon, technical information about the environmental conditions and the date of the closest match to their desired conditions in a two month interval. The user can view the Moon in first person to check for irregularities in the ground, and focus on the Sun and the Earth as they can be seen from the Moon's surface.

Apelle 11 addresses the challenge by combining the provided resources into one easy way to check all the relevant information of a landing site; it is important for regular citizens to have access to professional tools, and it is important for professional tools to be quick and easy to use, to help the productivity of experts around the world.
details:
Mode of operation

Apelle 11: Moon Landing Conditions Visualizer presents itself as a single screen upon which the user can find a 3D render of the Moon, the Sun and the Earth. The Moon is a 3D model with its ridges and craters represented, while the other two are smooth spheres. The render simulates the axis rotation of the Earth as well as the revolution of the Moon and the Earth. At any moment, the user can double click the Moon's surface to place themselves in first person view upon it; once there, they can choose to focus on the Earth or on the Sun to assess their position as seen from the surface of the Moon at that specific date and time.

Input

The user can input the following data:

  • Date and time: the user can input the desired date and time of the simulation, either through the date picker in the left side bar, or through the slider at the bottom of the screen. The simulation will match the selected date.
  • Landing site: the user can select a landing side from the left side bar (which shows possible Artemis III landing sites as per the Moon Trek website) or upload their own, in the format of a geojson file (an example is provided).
  • Azimuth and elevation: the user can provide their preferred conditions by stating their preferred elevation and azimuth for both the Earth and the Sun (as seen from the surface of the Moon).

Output

The overlay panel to the right of the screen will show the user technical information about their selected landing site, searching for the closest match to their preferred conditions in an interval of time from the selected date to two months after. It will display azimuth and elevation for both the Earth and the Sun, as well as the above mentioned closest matches to each of the four preferred conditions. It will add some important details:

  • Earth communication query window: the total time in which the Earth will be visible from the Moon landing site in the two month interval;
  • Communication window: the total time in which the Earth will be visible from the Moon landing site in a full day starting from the selected date and time.
  • Sunlight duration query window: the total time in which the Sun will be visible from the Moon landing site in the two month interval;
  • Sunlight window: the total time in which the Sun will be visible from the Moon landing site in a full day starting from the selected date and time.

Technologies

The following section will list the relevant technologies, divided by cathegory.

Development tools and environment

  • React - JavaScript library, used for ease of implementation of the UI;
  • PrimeReact - additional React library, used for premade components;
  • CesiumJS - Cesium JavaScript library for the 3D visualization of maps and globes, used to render the Moon, Sun and Earth models and their travel across the stars;
  • Node.js - JavaScript runtime environment for apps, used for the deployment of our github pages website;
  • GitHub - DVCS, used to synchronize the team and deploy our website through the Pages offer.

Data and resources

  • NASA websites (listed in the section below) for:
    • the Moon mosaic used in the CesiumJS render;
    • the geojson file containing Artemis III possible landing sites;
    • the ephemerides for the input conditions listed above;
    • all the images in the project slides.
  • Marshub website for the 3D model of the Moon complete with ridges and craters.

LLM usage

We used LLMs to better comprehend how to handle the NASA data and to understand which parts of it were significant to experts and curious explorers alike. We also wrote some of the code with the help of Claude and ChatGPT.

Considered factors

  • To guarantee the best communication, the azimuth and elevation where taken into account from all the points of the landing site polygon. Similarly, sunlight exposition was esteemed through the same indicators, following the intuitive idea that a visible Sun over the horizon meant more illumination.
  • The sunlight and communication factors are directly configurable by users, since we lacked the technical background needed to know which values would best fit the mission requirements.
  • The Moon's surface POV was added to intuitively show whether the Sun and Earth were visible from the landing site at a determined point in time.

Intended impact and provided benefits

  • Provide a simple and intuitive way to navigate dates and landing sites, while showing close-enough dates for the best landing dates, ranked with regard to the preferred settings for azimuth and elevation of both the Sun and the Earth.
  • An extensible platform that will allow more comparisons, for example, by showing which landing sites would best fit those requirements in a given time-period.
  • An intuitive and simplified interface for non-technical users, with an eye for UX and performant data-loading that does not overwhelm the user.

Future developments

The project could be updated in a number of ways, of which the most signifcant are the following:

  • Adding additional information about the surface of the Moon close to the selected landing site;
  • Allowing the user to derive a landing site from an input of preferred conditions and date, or the optimal date given a landing site and the required conditions.
